DILG BAGONG PIUPWAS Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA cor. Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City www.dilq.qov.ph OILG OPINION NO. S. 2020 MEMORANDUM TO SUBJECT DATE MARIA LOURDES L. AGUSTIN, CESO Ill Regional Director, DILG NCR LEGAL OPINION ON WHETHER THE PREVENTIVE SUSPENSION IMPOSED BY THE OFFICE OF THE OMBUDSMAN WILL SUBSIST DESPITE THE RE-ELECTION AND IMPENDING ASSUMPTION TO OFFICE OF THE AFFECTED SP MEMBERS [NCR-2025-06-11-004] JUL 0 1 2025 Reference: Your Memorandum dated June IO, 2025, seeking clarification on whether the preventive suspension imposed by the Office of the Ombudsman will subsist despite the re-election and impending assumption to office of the affected Sangguniang Panlungsod (SP) members In response thereto, we find it wise to revisit the nature of a preventive suspension. In Aldovino, Jr. vs. Commission on Electionsl, the Supreme Court exhaustively elucidated the same, thus: "Preventive suspension is imposed under the Local Government Code "when the evidence of guilt is strong and given the gravity of the offense, there is a possibility that the continuance in office of the respondent could influence the witnesses or pose a threat to the safety and integrity of the records and other evidence." Under the Anti-Graft and Corrupt Practices Act, it is imposed after a valid information (that requires a finding of probable cause) has been filed in court, while under the Ombudsman Act, it is imposed when, in the judgment of the Ombudsman, the evidence of guilt is strong; and (a) the charge involves dishonesty, oppression or grave misconduct or neglect in the performance of duty; or (b) the charges would warrant removal from the service; or (c) the respondent's continued stay in office may prejudice the case filed against him. Notably in all cases of preventive suspension, the suspended official is barred frbm performing the functions of his office and does not receive salary in the meanwhile, but does not vacate and lose title to his office; loss of office is a consequence that only results upon an eventual finding of guilt or liability." 1 G.R. No. 184836, December 232009. "Matino, Mahusay at Maaasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

In essence, a preventive suspension is a preliminary administrative measure intended to ensure the integrity of the investigation. Bearing in mind the nature of such a suspension, it is our submission that its enforcement cannot be nullified by mere re-election of a public official into office. Otherwise, allowing a re-elected official to immediately assume office sans fully serving the suspension order imposed by the Office of the Ombudsman would not only undermine the very purpose of such an administrative proceeding but also contradict a lawful mechanism put in place to ensure accountability. On that score, it behooves us to revisit the pronouncement of the Supreme Court in Carpio-Morales vs. Coutt of Appeals,2 where the Court abandoned the condonation doctrine. In the said case, the Court ratiocinated in this wise, thus: "[Tlhe concept of public office is a public trust and the corollary requirement of accountability to the people at all times, as mandated under the 1987 Constitution, is plainly inconsistent with the idea that an elective local official's administrative liability for a misconduct committed during a prior term can be wiped off by the fact that he was elected to a second term of office, or even another elective post. Election is not a mode of condoning an administrative offense, and there is simply no constitutional or statutory basis in our jurisdiction to support the notion that an official elected for a different term is fully absolved of any administrative liability arising from an offense done during a prior term." (Emphasis ours) Accordingly, re-election to office does not operate as a shield against administrative liability. Here, it is worth noting, however, that the aforesaid case involved administrative liability and not preventive suspension per se. At any rate, it is our submission that the underlying principle espoused therein is relevant. Thus, re-election of a sanggunian member does not preclude the continuation of the enforcement of a preventive suspension. Premised on the foregoing, we are of the view that preventive suspension issued by the Office of the Ombudsman remains enforceable even after re-election. This opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities or the courts. We hope to have guided you accordingly. BY AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: ATTY. ROMEO . BENITEZ Undersecretary for External, Legal and Legislative Affairs OUSELLNRPB/LLLS.LRALLD/jam 2 G.R. NO. 217126-27, November 10. 2015. Page 2 of 2
